propositions: Code review lacks a concurrency rubric and does not surface data races caused by inconsistent synchronization on shared resources

The concurrency overlay uses a two-tier deterministic lexical trigger: a committed high-precision tier (low noise, fires on explicit sync primitives) and a project-extensible noisy tier (via criteria_routing.json, catches project-modal races like unlocked git-index operations)
The overlay must be registered in the base reviewer catalog and implement a Pass-1 specialist prompt carrying the lockset-first rubric without model-emitted severity

Built-in committed triggers deliberately do not fire on this codebase's modal unlocked-twin races (raw git operations, getmtime-then-remove on lockfiles) by design; project-tier vocabulary in criteria_routing.json provides recall for those cases
The overlay ships advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) pending calibration, with documented blind spots: no-twin races and CI-level CAS/backoff races
Projects can extend any built-in overlay's trigger vocabulary and applies_to globs through criteria_routing.json without code changes
